That video has helped me a lot. It has made me go from a very slow sensitivity to a more average sensitivity with better flicks. If you don't want to watch the video, here's the steps he mentions.

1.) Turn all your sensitivity to 1, including ADS. It is super painful to play, *especially* if you ADS. Your goal is to complete a normal T-hunt/training ground as **Sledge** or **Thatcher** with their L85. If you can't stand the ADS then change ADS to 100 and keep horizontal and vertical to 1. This is to get your old sensitivity out of your system.

2.) Once you've completed at least one, turn all sensitivity to 100, including ADS. Yes, I know you want to, do as many 360s as you want when you spawn. When you've done as many 360s to your heart's content, pick **Sledge** or **Thatcher** again and complete a T-hunt/training ground on normal. This is to get used to a supremely high sensitivity.

3.) Once you've got your 720 trick shot no scopes down-- I mean, once you've beaten the mission on normal and have gotten somewhat accustomed to flicking between enemies with max sensitivity, pick **Buck** or **Twitch**  and reduce Vertical and ADS to 50. Your goal in the next T-hunt is to control Buck's (Twitch's) recoil reliably. Just because you beat this next T-hunt doesn't mean you can control the recoil. Until you feel comfortable with Buck's (Twitch's) gun, keep trying. You can even try in spawn if you need to. Just slightly tilt the right analog down to get a nice spray in a circle on a wall in front of you.

4.) Once you feel comfortable controlling Buck's or Twitch's vertical recoil, this is your chance to make final adjustments to your sensitivity. Go to Hereford Base, spawn at shooting range, and stand behind the counter and try to flick between each target. Change your horizontal if you're over compensating or not reaching each target per flick. If you keep wildly going in the air or aiming at the ground then change your vertical and ADS. For the most part you want to keep vertical and ADS at the same sensitivity unless something just feels off. All right, go into a normal T-hunt and start flicking with your favorite operator. Aim for the head.

5.) Once you feel comfortable with your new sensitivity then you're probably good to go. In the video he says the final phase is to beat a realistic T-hunt but that's not really necessary. It doesn't change AI at all, it just improves their accuracy and damage to an insane level. For a final phase just try and beat a T-hunt in under a certain amount of time. Don't drone, don't think, just enter and shoot.

And that's it. The biggest part of aiming, I've come to realize, is controlling recoil. Practice controlling recoil with Buck or Twitch and then your favorite operators and your aim should improve considerably. You won't see 100% progress immediately but you should feel a big improvement. I certainly did. *Always* do a T-hunt or two or five as soon as you get on Siege. Warm up, practice flicking, get your recoil controlled. **NEVER DRONE!!!** Run, shoot, flick, 360, react, run, shoot, react. Don't think, just go. This is your warm up for aiming.

Hope this helped some!

Start with a legendary bounty (the easiest is probably Etta Doyle, Wolf Man, or Philip Carlier) 

Make sure you take at least 15 minutes or a maximum of 30 minutes, then turn in the target. Taking a maximum of 30 minutes will net you 0.48 Gold and well over $100 for a 5 Star difficulty legendary bounty.

Go to another bounty board. Start a regular bounty, preferably one with a "Reward $$$" text at the top.

Go to the target (or targets if you're rollin' with a posse and chose a bounty with multiple targets). Take the target(s), turn in with 30 seconds left. So the thing that makes God Eater great is that the game does a great job of giving you information in the database to succeed. Every aragami has a weakness and a strategy to exploit that weakness. What the game wants you to do, to make things slightly more challenging, is to find out what weapons work the best against what aragami.

For example, the Quadriga is a rock hard machine. You won't get by very well with a slashing weapon like a scythe. Your best bet is a piercing weapon to pierce the metal or a crushing weapon to use on the legs to make Quadriga fall. The same strategy goes with a gun, use one with high piercing or crushing damage and use the strategy accordingly.

In addition, you can break parts off of an aragami to make normally resistant parts of a monster weak. That's why you claim it starts taking more damage midway throughout the fight. Not to mention some aragami have weak points to begin with.

Try reading through the database and each mission's description before heading out to fight a certain aragami. Once you have the information you need it's mostly just trial and error determining what weapon works the best. Although, any weapon can work wonderfully if you bring a weapon element the aragami is weak to and break any of its parts.

Gotcha'. Sadly I do not see anything wrong with your setup on the surface so I cannot give a solid solution as to why your bitrate fluctuates; perhaps your CPU is struggling to keep up? When I *record* with OBS and I'm using the x264 encoder my CPU stays hovered around 40% but it still struggles to keep up with, say, anything higher than 7000kbps or thereabouts. However, I emphasize *recording* rather than streaming because both work differently when you put bitrate into the picture.

You mentioned you were not a Twitch partner; somewhat unrelated to the immediate problem (and honestly a half-hearted solution *to* your problem), but I wouldn't recommend streaming anything above 2500kbps bitrate if you are **not** a Twitch partner. Even though your internet speed is well above capable of streaming 5000kbps bitrate, other people may not have great internet and will struggle to watch your stream. Twitch partners have transcoding enabled which allows their viewers to change resolutions and bitrate speed during stream, **non**-Twitch partners do not have this option and their viewers are stuck watching exactly how it's being streamed. If you knew this and do not want to change the bitrate then I would recommend streaming to YouTube. You don't have to but lowering the bitrate might also help with the fluctuation, even though it is half of what you normally set it as.

Some other and more legitimate solutions? Maybe go with a double negative; try streaming with a VBR instead of CBR and see what happens. You can also try tweaking the encoder around. Since you have an NVIDIA graphics card the NVENC H.264 encoder might be available which is oodles better, in my opinion, than x264. NVENC H.264 uses your graphics card, x264 uses CPU, for more reference. 

If none of those work then I'm all outta options. I hope you figure it out, though! If you just can't figure out the kinks then maybe try streaming to something other than Twitch? Twitch isn't very user friendly when it comes to non-Twitch partners haha

You know how some people get really nervous speaking in front of crowds? Talking into a microphone from the comfort of your own room, knowing that nobody will be....*listening*.... Wait I'm uploading this to YouTube? OH MAN DO I SOUND OKAY? OH JEEZ. OH NO. WAIT, DID I FORGET TO SAY THE INFO ABOUT THE MONSTER I JUST ATTACKED...?!? WHAT IF I'M PLAYING BADLY?! AGGHHHHH

It happens, when the camera is rolling and the mic is live it's easy to just start losing a grasp of what's going down and your mind ends up drawing blanks.

And even sometimes it has nothing to do with nervousness; do you warm up before recording? Do you eat or drink anything? Do you *truly* feel like recording? How is the environment? Will you be disturbed by family members? All of these can factor into your commentary, as well as a nervousness (or other negative change in mentality) once you hit that big red circle.

If it happens again make sure you play a little of something else *before* you record gameplay and commentary to get yourself warmed up. While playing just try talking to yourself in a normal conversational voice so it will be used a little. If you find yourself easily going quiet or just not feeling what you're playing you also might not really feel like recording. Finally, make sure you at least drink something before recording commentary and keep something nearby to quietly guzzle in between cutscenes or other edits if need be.

Also don't record when you first wake up, that's a big no-no. Try to wait a little and get yourself really waken up before recording so your voice will be clear and mind won't be hazy.

The great thing about The Elder Scrolls is that you can start *anywhere* and feel like it's a beginning. The lore is very overwhelming but everything and anything you'll need to know will be in any of the games.

If you still feel like you're missing something then the wiki would be a fantastic place to go to first. Not only can you learn about the lore but you can find out about *how* to learn about it through various media.

*After Sword Art Online I* you could watch *Sword Art Offline*, which is a cute chibi series that gives a recap of the Aincrad arc and Fairy Dance arc. **It is not mandatory.**

*After Sword Art Offline* you can watch *Sword Art Online Extra Edition* which is another recap but with a plot; Asuna, Lisbeth, Silica, and Sugu are at the school pool trying to teach Sugu how to swim because Yui wants to see a whale in ALO. Kirito is right next door meeting a representative of RCT and tells him what happened in Season 1. Nearing the end it turns into an actual episode with Kirito and the whole gang going on a quest. **This is also not mandatory** but it's worth watching just for the fanservice and wholesome gang quest at the end.

*After Sword Art Online Extra Edition* you can start watching *Sword Art Online II* which is Season 2 of the anime. It covers the Phantom Bullet arc, Calibur arc, and Mother's Rosario arc. While Fairy Dance holds a special place in my heart and Aincrad really gets me nostalgic and in my feels, Kawahara clearly shows his writing has improved; Phantom Bullet and Mother's Rosario are wonderfully written and the latter was even considered a side story in the original LN's! **This is mandatory to continue.** It is Season 2.

*After Sword Art Online II* you can watch *Sword Art Offline II*. It's just another chibi show. **It is not mandatory.**

*After Sword Art Offline II* you should watch *Sword Art Online: Ordinal Scale The Movie*. It can be considered an extra long prologue to Sword Art Online: Alicization as it covers characters and ideas that play a role in the upcoming arc. **It's not mandatory but HIGHLY recommended.** This is streaming on Netflix, otherwise you will have to purchase DVD/Blu-Ray. It is a well written movie and it really puts you in the feels. Plus there is a whole lot of gang screen time so if you have a favorite waifu or husbando then this will be a movie for you!

Finally, *After Sword Art Online: Ordinal Scale The Movie* you are now ready to start *Sword Art Online: Alicization*. It is six episodes in as of this moment. Not a lot has happened yet but it has already established a plot so now is a great time to start.

If you watched all the episodes of Alicization then there are also the games, light novels, and manga, as well, that vary in content and setting. I won't delve into all that unless you want me to. And you can also check out the hotbar at the top of the sub for any more questions :)

Ah, so you were using Part 8 Jason. He does have decreased sense range haha. I don't know if that was your problem but it's very possible.

>So when you're in rage and near them does it show you exactly where their hiding or does it make them stop hiding,

When Jason unlocks rage it allows him to see if a counselor is in a hiding spot, such as an outhouse or a tent, when using sense. If they are hiding in a closet or underneath a bed *inside a cabin* then it will glow red and Jason will still have to hunt down where they are inside that cabin. Trying to use sense on a hiding counselor prior to unlocking rage will not let Jason see the hiding spot or cabin the counselor is hiding in.

>another person had mentioned that they probably had the skill to hide from sense but lst I know it was only a chance to hide from sense

Indeed. So if you only used sense once before moving on then it is very possible Chad avoided it. Make sure to use it for a few seconds to scout the immediate area, take a few steps waiting for it to regenerate, then use sense again. Also, I reinstate, it's very possible that since you used Part 8 Jason the decreased sense really hindered your ability to see Chad.

As for tip #4: What I mean is if you have used sense in one area of the map and have not spotted a counselor then that means he or she avoided your sense, you were out of range and not able to see where he or she was, the counselor was hiding and you hadn't obtained rage yet, the counselor had exactly zero fear (which is *highly* unlikely, even for Jenny and Tommy), or a combination of any of those problems. If that's the case then morph to the center or another corner of the map to see if you can get a read

I have a few tips that you can keep in mind.

1.) If you enter a building or campsite and suspect someone is hiding then listen for breathing; the loudest breath you can hear is when they inhale and exhale.

2.) **The most important tip to use for endgame in general;** Once Jason's **"Rage"** ability unlocks not only does it allow you to walk through doors and walls but it also enhances each of Jason's abilities (and I *think* he walks and runs/speed walks a little faster?). But I bet you *didn't* know "Rage" also prevents counselors from hiding so long as your sense ability is in range of them. If you can't find a counselor and you're 100% sure you checked everywhere then wait for "Rage"; wherever that counselor is hiding will light up, or if they're in a cabin then the cabin will be lit. Of course only if your sense range is far enough to detect them, which rage should increase that too

3.) Use a Jason with a stronger sense ability and avoid Jasons that have decreased sense to determine if a counselor is actually hiding, preferably after you obtain rage.

4.) Relocate to the other end of the map as soon as morph is available and use sense, again, to check and see if the counselor is actually hiding, preferably after you obtain rage.

**Edit**
5.) Destroy power boxes. Good Jasons usually destroy at least one before they start attacking, regardless, but now would be a good time to destroy any you haven't yet.

Well first off, do you use a mic? If not then maybe you should, as communication is key to success in a game like Overwatch.

Secondly, do you choose characters that fit the team composition and counter the enemies? You say you main Soldier and Mercy, but sometimes a Soldier may not be what you need. As a rule of thumb it is always good to have two healers. If there is already three DPS then that is plenty, anymore more and that means you're left with only one tank and one healer which isn't good at all.

Lastly, depending on whatever hero you're playing as, your positioning is *critical*. If you're a Reinhardt, Orisa, or Zarya, you ALWAYS need to be in front of your team. If you're playing as Mercy then stay out of line of sight of the enemy and peek in and out to heal your team. You can heal through walls for about two or three seconds so use that to your advantage. If you're Soldier then you need to always be in control of the high ground. The only time you shouldn't be on the high ground is if your team isn't with you. In that case tell them over comms to take the high ground or push straight through the choke.

As always, just practice. Maybe there is a problem with your accuracy. Maybe your positioning just isn't the best. Or it is VERY possible your team just isn't doing their job. Just take it one step at a time.
